feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, relevant progression, and solid evidence of scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, tighter section consolidation, and a few consistency fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and experience align well around digital strategy, communications leadership, and platform modernization.  
- Strong credibility and progression: long tenure at NACo with promotions shows trust, growth, and increasing responsibility.  
- Good use of scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more results, not just responsibilities: include measurable outcomes such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, campaign results, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “workflows and systems”); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead. No major misspellings or typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads a bit generic and repeats several ideas already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with sharper positioning tied to senior leadership, public-sector/advocacy work, and platform transformation.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your seniority and niche: digital strategy leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter value proposition focused on cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, and operational systems.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, editorial and operational workflow design, and audience-focused content strategy across web, email, social, and multimedia. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear advocacy messaging and coordinating stakeholders across complex organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap heavily with Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination are repeated elsewhere; keep the intro high-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, resume-style nouns and avoid mixed constructions like “communication” vs. “coordination.”
- Prioritize strategic and senior-level strengths over generic execution terms.
- Consider rewrite: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Editorial operations & governance • Web platform & CMS leadership • Cross-channel communications • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder alignment & cross-functional leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- If space allows, replace “Web & CMS administration” with “Web platform & CMS leadership” to better match your seniority.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication,” “stakeholder & cross-department coordination,” and “policy & advocacy communication” repeat language already covered in the header and Soft Skills.
- This section also overlaps substantially with Topline Skills; keep Core Competencies broader and avoid tool-specific phrasing here.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and “Recent Projects.” Make it sharper by emphasizing this engagement’s highest-value outcomes and framing it as strategic + hands-on execution.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact and client context: “Embedded full-time as a strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-led bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line about improving cross-channel coordination and publishing efficiency.
- Make Drupal work more specific and results-oriented: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits for public-facing advocacy and engagement campaigns.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search relevance gains, or reduction in support issues.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI-enabled search, microsites, and anniversary/campaign work already appear in “Recent Projects”; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web modernization also echo the header and NACo role—avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with solid scale metrics; it should read more like an executive outcomes summary and less like a channel inventory. Emphasize transformation, team leadership, and measurable business results.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and multi-channel communications for a national membership organization.”
- Tighten and combine channel bullets; prioritize outcomes: website migration, analytics stack buildout, studio launch, and governance improvements.
- Add measurable results where possible: email engagement growth, social growth, production volume, reporting time saved, publisher adoption, or efficiency gains from governance changes.
- Consider a condensed rewrite:
  “Led NACo’s digital media team and enterprise digital strategy across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget. Directed redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers. Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio and expanded analytics infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to strengthen reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the earlier NACo role’s newsletter/social/video operations.
- Video-program expansion may duplicate the footer project list and prior NACo entries unless framed here as building organizational capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about hands-on operational leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth before the broader strategic remit of 2022–2024.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + distinction: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy, program and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points; combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show ownership and outcome: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” and “strengthened editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive strengths rather than repeating broad digital/comms language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content strategy” to sound more senior and aligned with director/consultant-level work.
- If space allows, make one line outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms” to reinforce scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header and Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact same wording.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is close to “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s currently a mixed list of platforms, methods, and tools with heavy overlap against “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize the most relevant web/CMS strengths and recent execution themes.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a sharper, grouped line: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search
- Consider replacing “Technical Execution” with “Web Platforms & CMS Delivery” to sound more outcome-oriented and less generic.
- Keep higher-value, recent capabilities first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, API/workflow automation.
- If possible, align wording to recent experience: e.g., “CMS modernization & migration” instead of just “CMS modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and recent project language; keep here only if shortened.
- Most items repeat the “Technical + IT” section, so this topline version should stay selective, not exhaustive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability over repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools and group them: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten the tail end: change “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and performance optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive reporting dashboards • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; use Topline Skills for higher-level strengths, not another software list.
- “Leadership reporting” may be better phrased as “executive reporting” for stronger, more standard wording.

Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing production environment and delivery scope rather than repeating broad video terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery**

- “Video production and editing” overlaps with Technical + IT (“Premiere Pro… Podcast production”) and multiple work-experience bullets.
- “Livestreaming” duplicates Core Competencies; use “livestream and hybrid event delivery” to add specificity.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same CMS names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level/relevance, e.g. “Drupal (primary; enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Put the most relevant platform first and consider dropping lower-signal tools if space is tight: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages.
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses rather than just names: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint.”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; “GitHub Pages” may fit better under technical implementation than CMS.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- “Drupal” is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating it without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support your recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Front-End, Tagging & Automation” to make the category more specific and less repetitive.
- Use cleaner phrasing and modernize terms: “HTML/CSS” instead of “HTML5/CSS3”; keep “JavaScript”; remove “jQuery” unless still actively used in recent work.
- Group by function for readability: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”.
- If accurate, add scope/level in parentheses rather than more tools, e.g., “API integrations (REST)” or “GitHub Actions (deployment workflows)”.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same wording in both places.
- “Workflow automation” is also covered elsewhere, so GitHub Actions should stay framed as technical delivery, not general automation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems
- Group by function for faster scanning: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “workflow automation, project coordination, and cross-team communications”
- Consider trimming weaker/older tools if not used recently; keep the most relevant to current consulting and director-level operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; if space is tight, prioritize automation/project systems over basic comms platforms

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it reads as a vendor list rather than a skills signal. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize platform breadth and campaign/engagement systems without restating newsletter management.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform names for readability: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one capability cue to increase value: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • email automation / journey orchestration
- Keep this item concise and tool-focused; save outcomes like audience size, newsletter volume, or campaign impact for the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 experience bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or “multi-channel communications” here; those are already covered in Core Competencies and recent NACo experience.
- If Dynamics 365 was only lightly used, consider dropping it to avoid overstating depth versus stronger platforms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but it reads broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make this item more foundational: emphasize team build-out, early channel operations, and concrete outputs rather than repeating later leadership themes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to focus on early-career scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add specific outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, weekly video cadence, audience growth, or process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with action + result.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows across web, email and social. Provided direct guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; differentiate this as launching/producing the series rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating governance/operations language already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the distinctive “firsts,” cross-functional coordination, and any concrete outputs or audiences.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and policy research initiatives for NACo programs while supporting digital storytelling and multimedia communications.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add scale or outcomes: number of episodes, internal stakeholders supported, programs/policy areas covered, or audience/download metrics.
- Consider a sharper version: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research coordination and digital content production; launched NACo’s first podcast and managed end-to-end editorial and production workflow.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production and multimedia materials” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video/multimedia generally; the podcast launch is the unique differentiator here.
